name: Krypton
occurrence: Trace component of the atmosphere (about 1 part per million), extracted from liquefied air.
majorUses: High-performance camera flash and stadium lighting
notableCharacteristics: One of the few noble gases that can be coaxed into forming real compounds (like KrF₂) under extreme conditions, despite its 'inert' reputation.
whyHere: Although its full octet makes bonding rare, krypton's larger, more loosely held outer electrons make it slightly more reactive than lighter noble gases — just enough to form unstable compounds like KrF₂ under extreme lab conditions.
didYouKnow: From 1960 to 1983, the metre was officially defined using a specific wavelength of light emitted by krypton-86 atoms, before the definition switched to the speed of light instead.
genZNote: Not actually Superman's home planet's namesake for chemistry reasons, but it did briefly define the entire metric system's metre.
